purpose: Conditional non-actionable context rolls after selected external-cause ICD outcomes. These rolls never alter mortality or cause selection.

CA.label: Canada
CA.provenance: Toronto pre-barrier annual means provide the Canada top-level split: 38.5 building jumps versus 9.3 at Bloor Street Viaduct plus 8.7 at other bridges. Building subtypes are distributed using Chen, Gunnell & Lu (Taipei) proportions normalized across their four reported building categories. Model-normalized site-type roll.
CA.model_status: Canada-native top-level split + international building-subtype reference

INTL_REFERENCE.label: International jumping-site reference
INTL_REFERENCE.provenance: Equal blend of the Toronto pre-barrier building-versus-bridge split and the Swiss national report's approximate two-thirds-building/one-third-bridge pattern; building subtypes use Chen, Gunnell & Lu (Taipei) proportions normalized across their four reported building categories. No height, named hotspot or access information is modeled.

all.provenance: Primary-agent counts from 684 fatal poisonings in Northern Finland, 2007-2011: antidepressants 48, neuroleptics 32, benzodiazepines 26, antiepileptics 20; normalized over these X41-compatible classes. Statistics Finland separately reports tranquilliser/sleeping-medicine poisonings, especially benzodiazepines, as a major accidental-poisoning group.
all.model_status: Finnish regional primary-agent evidence; not a nationwide X41-only cross-tab

male.provenance: PHAC national coroner/medical-examiner chart review, 2016-2017. Sex-specific counts identified as causing death are normalized across X41-compatible classes: benzodiazepines plus Z-drugs, tricyclic plus other antidepressants, antipsychotics, and gabapentinoids.
male.model_status: Canada national sex-specific evidence-weighted X41-compatible class model

female.provenance: PHAC national coroner/medical-examiner chart review, 2016-2017. Sex-specific counts identified as causing death are normalized across X41-compatible classes: benzodiazepines plus Z-drugs, tricyclic plus other antidepressants, antipsychotics, and gabapentinoids.
female.model_status: Canada national sex-specific evidence-weighted X41-compatible class model

all.provenance: PHAC national coroner/medical-examiner chart review, Canada 2016-2017. Among accidental acute-toxicity deaths, the published distribution of the number of substance types identified as causing death was 29% one substance, 7% unknown, and therefore 64% two or more substances at the published whole-percent resolution. Applied to X44 only as a labeled accidental-acute-toxicity reference for substance-count context; it is not an X44-specific cross-tab and does not identify exact molecules.
all.model_status: Canada national accidental acute-toxicity reference; not X44-specific

FI.label: Finland | OTI fatal motor-vehicle crashes 2015-2024
FI.provenance: OTI road-accident investigation-board review, 2015-2024: 1,474 fatal motor-vehicle crashes. 526 were caused by impaired drivers. Among those 526: alcohol only n=263, alcohol plus another intoxicant n=118, other intoxicant without alcohol n=139, and n=6 could not be classified due to incomplete information. Figure 1 gives 890 crashes caused by clear drivers and 58 with impairment information unavailable. Percent calculations in the report use cases with required information; this model preserves the unknown category instead of dropping it.
FI.model_status: Finland national fatal-crash investigation reference; crash-level, not decedent-specific

CA.label: Canada | fatal-collision contributing factors | 2022
CA.provenance: Transport Canada, Canadian Motor Vehicle Traffic Collision Statistics 2022: impaired / under the influence was reported as a contributing factor in 23.0% of fatal collisions in 2022. Contributing factors can overlap, and the published estimates use submissions from a subset of provinces and territories. Absence from this roll is therefore not a claim that every involved person was sober.
CA.model_status: Canada national subset-estimated fatal-collision contributing-factor reference; crash-level
